correctness.rationale: The cyclic difference set D={1,3,4,5,9} gives a symmetric 2-(11,5,2) design with 22 point/block vertices and 55 incidences; distances are 2 within each part and 1 or 3 across parts. At scale two the point simplex plus union of block stars are both contractible with intersection the block complex L, hence K2≃ΣL. Direct independent construction of L yields f=(11,55,110,55,11), and 55 actual free-face elementary collapses leave a two-complex f=(11,55,66). An independently selected set of 45 triangular relators eliminates all 45 non-tree loops, proving pi1(L)=1; Euler characteristic then gives H2=Z^21 and L≃wedge21 S2 by Hurewicz/Whitehead. Suspension yields wedge21 S3. K1 connected 55-edge graph gives 34 loops and K3 simplex. Signed Lefschetz of C11 translations gives H1 character 34 at identity and 1 otherwise, H3 character 21 at identity and −1 otherwise, yielding (4,3) and (1,2) rational irreducible multiplicities. Full 55-collapse and 45-relator enumerations are exhaustive and were reconstructed independently; original submitted certificate was inspected as source evidence, not accepted as proof by a log.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for an exact, naturally selected 11-point design Rips filtration and rational cyclic character. Alavi–Daneshkhah–Praeger classify biplanes and their automorphisms but not incidence-graph Vietoris–Rips homotopy. Virk general Dowker/Rips nerve equivalences make the reduction a standard method, not this computed 21-sphere wedge or representation. Feng–Nukala calculate symmetric-difference finite metric complexes, not the biplane metric. Resultary projective-plane and affine-plane incidence Rips results require different block intersection counts; the projective-plane lambda=1 theorem does not imply biplane lambda=2. The unique eleven-point biplane is a mathematically motivated natural finite design.
residual_risks: Full-text search of all older Rips computations on Hadamard biplanes was not exhaustive.
No extension to other symmetric designs, full automorphism groups, or integral C11-module splitting is claimed.
